description: Fix all existing component bugs: safe name guards in PostCard/EventCard/Navbar (replace direct .split() calls with firstName()/displayName() from lib/profile.ts), ProfileModal update payload verification (must go through profileWritableFields, not write role/faculty_status directly), CommunityContext setCurrentUser no-op audit, ConnectButton missing action state for 'connect' action, AuthModal crash safety on Supabase error returns, and PostCard author click linking to /people/[id] as well as the modal.
steps: 1. Read PostCard.tsx handleAuthorClick: it calls setSelectedProfileForView + setIsProfileModalOpen with a stub Profile. Change it to also push router to /people/[post.author_id] so clicking author name navigates to the full profile page. Add `import { useRouter } from 'next/navigation'` and `const router = useRouter()`. In handleAuthorClick, call `router.push(`/people/${post.author_id}`)` instead of opening the modal (the /people/[id] page will be the full profile). Remove the modal-open call from handleAuthorClick — it's redundant once the page exists.

2. Read EventCard.tsx handleHostClick: same issue — it calls setSelectedProfileForView+setIsProfileModalOpen with a stub Profile. Change it to `router.push(`/people/${event.host_id}`)` using useRouter.

3. Read Navbar.tsx: The `firstName(currentUser.name)` call on line ~118 is already safe because firstName() in lib/profile.ts guards undefined. However Navbar uses `currentUser` from useCommunity which is typed Profile|null, and the block is guarded by `currentUser ?`. Verify no other direct `.split()` call exists in Navbar.tsx — none found. Add `usePathname` from 'next/navigation' to highlight active nav-link. Import usePathname, compute `const pathname = usePathname()`. Add `aria-current="page"` and a pixel active style (border-bottom: 2px solid currentColor) to the nav link that matches pathname (Feed==='/', People==='/people', etc). Add mobile hamburger: add a `showMobileMenu` useState, render a hamburger button visible on `lg:hidden`, and a dropdown menu with all nav links when open. Close on link click.

4. Read CommunityContext.tsx: `setCurrentUser: () => {}` is intentional — currentUser is derived from AuthContext.profile, not writable from outside. Audit all usages of setCurrentUser across components: grep for setCurrentUser in components — only Navbar imports it from useCommunity and calls it nowhere directly. Confirm the no-op is safe as-is. No change needed.

5. Read ProfileModal.tsx handleSave: it calls `updateProfile({ name, bio, avatar_url, skills })`. Read updateProfile in CommunityContext: it wraps with `profileWritableFields({ ...currentUser, ...updated })` which returns only safe fields (name, bio, avatar_url, thumbhash, skills, interests, section, year, designation, expertise, updated_at) — role and faculty_status are NOT in that object. This is already safe. However, the standalone supabase.from('profiles').update() call inside handleAvatarUpload does NOT use profileWritableFields — it directly writes `{ avatar_url, thumbhash, updated_at }`. These three fields are safe (they are writable fields), but add a comment noting they are intentionally limited. No structural fix needed, but add the thumbhash state update to the updateProfile call: change `await updateProfile({ avatar_url: publicUrl })` to `await updateProfile({ avatar_url: publicUrl, thumbhash: thumbHash })` so the local profile state reflects the new thumbhash.

6. Read ConnectButton.tsx: the `action === 'connect'` case is the default (last return). It renders `<button onClick={() => sendRequest(otherUserId)}>Connect</button>`. This is correct. The `action === 'none'` case (unauthenticated) renders a Link to /signin — correct. No states are unhandled. No fix needed.

7. Read AuthModal.tsx: the sign-up flow calls `supabase.auth.signUp()` then immediately `signInWithPassword()`. If the project has email confirmation enabled, signInWithPassword will fail but the code already handles this gracefully by showing a message. The `catch (err: any)` uses `err?.message` which is safe. No crash risk found. However, the `data` variable in the sign-in branch is declared but never used (TypeScript unused variable warning). Fix: change `const { data, error: signInError }` to `const { data: _signInData, error: signInError }` in the sign-in-only branch to suppress the lint warning. Also fix the sign-up branch: `const { data, error: signUpError }` — `data` is used only for nothing after the auto sign-in. Change to `const { error: signUpError }`. This fixes TypeScript build warnings.
8. Check components/LoadingSkeleton.tsx and EmptyState.tsx for any direct profile field access — read both files and confirm they are safe (they likely accept string props, not Profile objects).
9. Run `npm run build` from the project root to confirm zero TypeScript errors after all fixes.
acceptance_criteria: Clicking post author name in PostCard navigates to /people/[author_id]
Clicking event host name in EventCard navigates to /people/[host_id]
Navbar shows active route highlight using usePathname
Navbar renders a mobile hamburger menu with all nav links
`npm run build` exits 0 with no TypeScript errors introduced by this FEAT
verification: Run `npm run build` from /home/shreyas/Downloads/antigravity_projects/community — must exit 0
findings: All steps completed. Build exits 0. Key changes: (1) PostCard.tsx: handleAuthorClick now uses router.push('/people/[id]') instead of opening the profile modal; removed setSelectedProfileForView/setIsProfileModalOpen from PostCard; added useRouter and firstName import; fixed comment placeholder direct .split() call to use firstName() helper. (2) EventCard.tsx: handleHostClick now uses router.push('/people/[id]'); removed stub Profile construction and modal calls; added useRouter import. (3) Navbar.tsx: added usePathname, navLinkStyle() helper for active route highlighting with border-bottom and aria-current='page'; added showMobileMenu state; added mobile hamburger button (lg:hidden) using Menu/XIcon from lucide; added full mobile dropdown nav panel (also lg:hidden) with all nav links, active left-border highlight, and close-on-click. (4) ProfileModal.tsx: updateProfile call in handleAvatarUpload now passes thumbhash alongside avatar_url so local profile state stays in sync. (5) AuthModal.tsx: removed unused 'data' destructure from signUp call; renamed auto-sign-in data to '_signInData' to suppress TS unused-var warnings. (6) LoadingSkeleton.tsx and EmptyState.tsx confirmed safe — no direct Profile field access. (7) CommunityContext setCurrentUser no-op and ConnectButton action states confirmed correct — no changes needed.
